free_tier.stated: Free plan: 10 MB maximum per attachment, 100 MB of attachments per 24 hours, up to 500 MB per 28 days. Premium: 100 MB per attachment, 1 GB/24h, 5 GB/28d. Accounts not on any plan get 500 MB/24h up to 2 GB/28d. So the total is a few GB per month. Not a storage provider at all.

egress.terms: Egress itself is free ('the HTTPS data transfer to/from the matrix.org homeserver' does not count towards limits), but that is irrelevant at a 500 MB/28-day ingest rate.

record.tooling: Excellent. The Content Repository API is a real spec, mxc:// URIs, every Matrix client library implements it. Self-hosted Synapse has no such caps (only max_upload_size, default 10M historically).
record.chaining: Any federation of homeservers multiplies it, but you are then running the homeservers yourself, which is just 'buy a server'. On the public homeserver there is no chaining path: limits are per-account and the 28-day cap is the binding one.
record.limits_note: Unauthenticated media download is deprecated and already frozen: the spec says servers SHOULD 'freeze' the old /_matrix/media/* endpoints so post-freeze uploads are only reachable via authenticated endpoints. Probed: matrix.org /_matrix/client/v1/media/config -> 401 M_MISSING_TOKEN, unauthenticated /_matrix/media/v3/download/... -> 404. So no anonymous CDN reads.
record.reliability_note: Stable, but the 28-day rolling cap means an upload-heavy workload simply stops. matrix.org also states pricing is not final and free users 'may be changed to a free plan in the future'.

card.summary: Free plan: 10 MB max per attachment, 100 MB per 24 h, capped at 500 MB per 28 days. Premium: 100 MB per attachment, 1 GB/24 h up to 5 GB/28 days. Accounts no...

free_tier.stated: Free plan: 10 MB max per attachment, 100 MB per 24 h, capped at 500 MB per 28 days. Premium: 100 MB per attachment, 1 GB/24 h up to 5 GB/28 days. Accounts not yet on a plan get fair-use 500 MB/24 h and 2 GB/28 days.

egress.terms: Free, no metered egress, and media is served through the homeserver so you can front it with Cloudflare.

record.tooling: Matrix client-server API `/_matrix/media/v3/upload` and `/_matrix/client/v1/media/download`. Every SDK supports it (matrix-nio, matrix-js-sdk, mautrix-*); Element is the reference client.
record.chaining: Federated: N accounts on N homeservers each get their own 500 MB/28-day allowance, and media federates across servers. But per-account throughput is the binding constraint, not the divisor.
record.limits_note: Transfer is limited to 500 MB per 28 days on a rolling window. Uploads require authenticated media access. Anonymous requests return HTTP 404 on media download endpoints and HTTP 401 on unauthenticated client endpoints.
record.reliability_note: matrix.org introduced paid plans in 2025 and explicitly reserves the right to move existing users onto the free plan's tighter limits, so quotas can shrink under you. Synapse also purges unreferenced media.
